newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end lower on U.S. rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end lower on U.S. rate fears.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended a dull session lower on Thursday as U.S. inflation fears pressured interest rates there and forced most investors to the sidelines of emerging markets.

"The market was dull again, most trading was by locals. We are treading water until the Fed meeting next week," a trader said, referring to the September 25 U.S. Federal Reserve meeting to set U.S. interest rate policy.
The blue chip IPC index closed down 20.64 points, or 0.61 percent, at 3,348.36. Volume was thin at 57.1 million shares. There were 56 losers and 27 gainers.
Traders said activity was dominated by same-day buying and selling of undervalued and infrequently traded stocks, typical of sessions with low volume.

Gainers were headed by paper company Kimber and bottler Grupo Continental, but with low volume trades. Much more substantial was buying in insurance firm Invecop, which dealers said was due to technical and speculative buying in what is not normally an active issue.
Similarly, the first four percentage losers were all traded at wafer-thin volume. Bottler Gemex B shares fell 9.09 percent on just 1,000 shares traded.
Analysts said weak volume reflected unease among foreign investors about the Mexican market, despite an improving economic picture in Mexico.
"Some foreigners sold stocks here to invest in the U.S. bond market ... maybe they thought they were better off there," said a Mexico City analyst.
These sales helped weaken the 48-hour peso by three centavos to 7.526/7.53 per dollar at the close, he added.
